question: Should `chat.send` adopt eager transcript persistence as its canonical durability boundary, or should the latency problem be solved through the current session/queue design instead?
rationale: The PR changes the observable timing and ownership of durable user-turn persistence across gateway, queue, and Pi session paths; the correct long-term contract cannot be selected from an old, conflicted branch alone.

options.title: Sponsor a current-main port
options.body: Keep eager persistence as the intended direction, but require a rebase plus focused proof for busy same-session, rollover, and duplicate-suppression behavior.

options.title: Choose another durability boundary
options.body: Retain the existing send contract and pursue a queue/session-owner solution that resolves latency without moving transcript persistence into the gateway send path.

options.title: Close the stale implementation
options.body: Close this branch if no owner wants to adopt the cross-layer durability contract, while preserving the related WebChat reliability reports for a narrower future fix.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a current-main port
recommendation.body: Keep eager persistence as the intended direction, but require a rebase plus focused proof for busy same-session, rollover, and duplicate-suppression behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the proposed implementation details and can supply a current-main port, though a repository owner must make the contract decision.
